candidate_relations.label: Hodgkin lymphoma, recurrence
candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is myxoinflammatory fibroblastic sarcoma (MIFS), a soft-tissue sarcoma characterized by myxoid stroma, inflammatory infiltrate, lipoblast-like cells, and Reed–Sternberg–like cells that are IHC-negative for lymphoid markers. Hodgkin lymphoma recurrence is a related differential (explaining why IHC was recommended) but represents an incompatible diagnostic entity with different lineage, treatment, and prognosis. The clinical and histologic context—acral soft-tissue mass with myxoid gelatinous gross appearance and fibroblastic spindle cells—favors MIFS over lymphoma recurrence.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hodgkin lymphoma recurrence is a lymphoid neoplasm; myxoinflammatory fibroblastic sarcoma is a distinct soft-tissue sarcoma entity

case_quality_flags: Reed–Sternberg–like cells in MIFS are a known diagnostic pitfall mimicking Hodgkin lymphoma; IHC differentiation is clinically appropriate and well-documented in the record
